title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: ARLO'S ICE RINK
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Arlo Jensen, a Zamboni driver from Fargo, North Dakota.
For thirty years, he has kept the ice at the old Northside rink smooth as glass.
Then a notice said the rink would close in March, unless somebody found two hundred thousand dollars.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE PICKLE JAR
segments.quote: It is the greatest of all mistakes to do nothing because you can only do little.
segments.author: Sydney Smith
lines: Arlo had about four hundred dollars, and a truck whose heater works on Tuesdays.
Then he remembered a line on his mom's fridge, from the English writer Sydney Smith:
It is the greatest of all mistakes to do nothing because you can only do little.
So he did a little. A pickle jar by the skate counter. Save our ice.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE MEETING
segments.quote: Talent wins games, but teamwork and intelligence wins championships.
segments.author: Michael Jordan
lines: But the hockey moms, the figure skaters and the old-timers had fought over ice time for years.
On the locker room wall hung a faded Michael Jordan poster:
Talent wins games, but teamwork and intelligence wins championships.
So Arlo called one meeting, with free coffee. They argued for an hour, then planned a skate-a-thon. Together.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE SLUSH
segments.quote: If there is no struggle, there is no progress.
segments.author: Frederick Douglass
lines: A week before the big night, the old cooling machine died. The ice turned to gray slush.
Arlo wanted to quit. Ruth from the snack bar pointed at a poster of Frederick Douglass:
If there is no struggle, there is no progress.
So Arlo crawled behind that machine with two retired mechanics. By Sunday, the ice was back.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE FALL
segments.quote: Our greatest glory is not in never falling, but in rising every time we fall.
segments.author: Oliver Goldsmith
lines: On opening night, Arlo stepped out to give a speech, and fell flat on his back.
Lying there, he remembered the Irish writer Oliver Goldsmith:
Our greatest glory is not in never falling, but in rising every time we fall.
He got up, took a bow, and said, that was the warm-up. The crowd roared.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE COSTUME
segments.quote: Do not take life too seriously. You will never get out of it alive.
segments.author: Elbert Hubbard
lines: At three in the morning, the pledges slowed down.
Ruth held up a sparkly skating outfit and read from Elbert Hubbard, an old American writer:
Do not take life too seriously. You will never get out of it alive.
So Arlo, all two hundred and forty pounds of him, put it on and did one slow spin.
The video went all over Fargo. The pledges doubled.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: MAIN STREET
segments.quote: Don't give up. Don't ever give up.
segments.author: Jim Valvano
lines: By March, they were still twelve thousand dollars short.
Arlo thought of the famous speech by basketball coach Jim Valvano:
Don't give up. Don't ever give up.
So he drove the Zamboni down Main Street with the pickle jar on the hood.
People emptied their pockets. They made it, with forty dollars to spare.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Do a little. Work together. Push through. Get back up. Laugh. Don't quit.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Do a little. Work together. Push through. Get back up. Laugh. And don't ever quit.
I tried a spin on the ice once. The ice won.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
